full_judgment:
8. The learned Judge of the High Court Division found that the admitted position was that 1.60 acres of land was mortgaged by Abdul Hamid to the defendants' predecessors, Badiuddin and Nazu Mia, by executing two mortgage deeds, Exts, B and BI, on 16-6-1919 for a period of 5 years. The learned Judge then found that the plaintiff or his predecessor-in-interest Abdul Hamid was at liberty to file a regular suit for possession and redemption instead of taking recourse to section 266 of the Bengal Tenancy Act for the said purpose. The learned Judge observed that the present suit was filed by the plaintiff who is an heir of the mortgagor Abdul Hamid for declaration of his title and confirmation of possession, in the alternative, for recovery possession and "there is no bar against treating this suit for redemption of the mortgage entered into by Abdul Hamid." The learned Judge then went on to consider whether the suit was filed within the period of limitation i.e. 60 years under article 148 of the Limitation Act. The mortgages were for 5 years i.e. from 16-6-1919 and, as such, the learned Judge found that they were extinguished after the expiry of 15-6-1924 and consequently the cause of action for a suit for redemption or for recovery of Khas possession of the lands under Exts. B and BI accrued on 16-6-1924. The present suit having been filed on 8-12-82, it was well within 60 years from the date of accrual of the cause of action and as such the suit was not barred by limitation, the learned Judge held. 

 9. The learned Judge then observed that since by operation of sub-section (5) of section 266 of the Bengal Tenancy Act the mortgage of 1.60 acres of land by Abdul Hamid in favor of the predecessors-in-interest of the contesting defendants under the deeds of mortgage Exts. B and B(1) had been extinguished and the suit was not barred by limitation and being within time, the plaintiff is entitled to redeem the said mortgages and get khas possession of the said land. 

 10. The learned Judge, however, went on to observe that although it had been decided that the plaintiff was entitled to redeem the aforesaid 1.60 acres of land, the suit could not be decreed granting recovery of khas possession of the entire disputed land i.e. 3.32 acres in the absence of any finding by the Courts below whether Jamaluddin had subsisting interest in his -/8/ annas share and whether the said share devolved on the plaintiff by purchase from the heirs of Jamaluddin as alleged in the plaint. The learned Judge observed that although the plaintiff had been found to be entitled to get declaration of his title in 1.60 acres of land by redeeming the mortgage, the suit must be remitted to the trial Court for coming to a finding as to whether the plaintiff had acquired title in the share of Jamaluddin as it appeared that there was no sufficient evidence on the point for which it was not possible for the High Court Division to make any finding regarding the share of Jamaluddin. 

 12. Although leave was obtained against the order of remand raising two grounds, Khandkar Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate for the appellants, who appeared at the hearing of the appeal, modified his submission by stating that the order of remand insofar as it relates to the determination of the plaintiff's alleged title to the -/8/- annas share to Jamaluddin cannot be opposed except that the parties should not be allowed to lead oral evidence after such a long time. Mr. Ahmed, however, submitted that documentary evidence, if any, should be allowed to be proved and so much of oral evidence as may be necessary to prove the same may also be allowed. Mr. Ahmed's main contention is that the learned Judge of the High Court Division acted illegally in holding that the plaintiff was entitled to the declaration of title to and recovery of khas possession of the mortgaged land (1.60 acres) upon treating the present suit as a suit for redemption of mortgage and that also without there being a prayer on behalf of the plaintiff for amendment of the plaint. Mr. Ahmed argued with emphasis that the High Court Division made a fundamental mistake in not noticing that the course adopted by the learned Judge had changed the nature and character of the suit i.e. changing a simple Title suit with prayer for confirmation or in the alternative for recovery of possession into a suit for redemption of mortgage, which is a class apart, causing great prejudice to the defendant-appellants. Mr. Ahmed submitted that the High Court Division without at all considering the defendants' case as regards the mortgaged land (1.60 acres) as set out in the written statement and supported by evidence committed a substantial error in holding that the plaintiff was entitled to a decree for declaration of title upon redemption of mortgage.
